text:
sarah: heads-up — we discovered a tenant snapshot that was copied into another account last night. not yet sure if it was manual or a script. copying here for visibility and next steps. anyone oncall?

mike: oncall here. details? which snapshot id and which bucket/account?

sarah: snapshot id snap-2026-03-20-22, destination account 908112233445, S3 path s3://redwood-exports/tenants/tenant-alpha/snap-2026-03-20.gz :thinking_face:

anita: is the snapshot encrypted with customer CMK or platform CMK?

sarah: looks like platform CMK (arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01). source metadata missing tenant_cmk tag. uploading service account `backup-uploader` did the copy.

mike: OK — two issues: 1) cross-account copy of snapshot (policy question) 2) platform CMK used instead of per-tenant CMK (data separation/compliance). recommend immediate ACL block on that S3 path and audit log export.

encops-bot: Alert: S3ObjectCopy detected from bucket redwood-prod-db-snapshots to redwood-exports by service-account backup-uploader at 2026-03-20T22:14:03Z. KMS key used: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01. Reaction: :eyes:

jordan: if we block the path we might break restores for that uploader. can we restrict just the copied object or revoke the specific upload key?

anita: yes, create a short-lived deny on s3:PutObject for the object prefix and also request immediate KMS grant revocation for the uploader role. steps: 1) apply S3 object lock on that key (or deny). 2) add a conditional deny to the uploader role

mike: proposal for RBAC change (short term): add explicit deny statement into backup-uploader role for s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::redwood-exports/tenants/* unless request includes tag tenant=owner. Also remove broad kms:Encrypt permission for platform key from that role. Long term: require per-tenant CMKs for tenant snapshots and enforce via policy validator.

sarah: can someone run the quick commands? i can patch the bucket policy but not the KMS grants.

anita: i'll handle KMS. revoke the DataKeyGenerate grant for backup-uploader: run
```bash
aws kms retreive-grants --key-id abcd-ef01 
# then: aws kms revoke-grant --key-id abcd-ef01 --grant-id <grant-id> --region us-west-2
```
(note: typo in tool name above — use `list-grants` then `revoke-grant`)

mike: i'll apply the temporary IAM deny. snippet: 
```json
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Action": "s3:PutObject",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-exports/tenants/*",
  "Condition": {"StringNotEquals": {"s3:RequestObjectTag/tenant":"${aws:PrincipalTag/tenant}"}}
}
```

jordan: do we have audit logs showing who authorized the cross-account copy? need to know if this was an exploited credential or a misconfigured automation.

sarah: checking CloudTrail now. preliminary shows assume-role by `backup-uploader` from ec2:backup-runner at 2026-03-20T22:12:50Z followed by s3:CopyObject. no console signins.

anita: marking this as vuln-triage P2 until we confirm intent. action items: [sarah: preserve object, disable further copies; mike: apply IAM deny; anita: revoke kms grant + rotate platform key if necessary; jordan: audit CloudTrail + notify compliance].

mike: one more: if platform key is rotated, we must ensure existing snapshots remain decryptable for restores. we may need to re-encrypt exported snapshots with tenant CMK or a wrap key. coordinate with storage team.

encops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-031. Owner: anita. SLA: 24h. Links: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-031

sarah: thanks team. i'll take a snapshot-preservation backup to a quarantined bucket and tag it `investigation=true` before deny goes in. will post command when done. :thumbsup:
